attempts.label: DANDI:001260
attempts.paper_title: A prefrontal cortex map based on single-neuron activity
attempts.entry_title: A prefrontal cortex map from single-neuron activity (Le Merre, Heining et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Here is the paragraph so it can be saved as that file: Most descriptive findings hold up in this data, but the hierarchy findings could not be tested and two cross-region claims did not reproduce. Wide and narrow waveform classes, higher rates in narrow-spiking units, regular firing in prefrontal cortex, stable firing categories over time, and prefrontal subregion maps all reproduced. Correlations of firing categories with the cortical hierarchy, and the ILA-specific activity module, stayed undecided because the paper gives no rule for numbering categories on a retrained map. The match between narrow and wide units across regions and the high-rate tone-responsive result did not reproduce. The replication on International Brain Laboratory data was too large to attempt.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Le Merre, Heining et al. (2026) on dandiset 001260, which holds 74 of the 99 Neuropixels recordings of the paper's dataset KI (the other 25 are in dandiset 000473). It recomputes the spontaneous firing metrics, the self-organizing map categories, their stability and their enrichment across brain regions, layers and the PFC flatmap, the Harris and Gao hierarchy correlations and the tone-response categories. The claims on the International Brain Laboratory data are not tested.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Le Merre, Heining et al. (2026) from dandiset 001260

outcomes.statement: Dataset KI holds 24,248 single units from 99 Neuropixels recordings in awake head-fixed mice, 52% of them in the PFC and 48% in other brain regions.
outcomes.source: Results, Capturing the diversity of spontaneous firing patterns, paragraph 1; Methods, Unit quality control
outcomes.quote: We recorded the firing activity of 24,248 single units from awake, head-fixed mice (dataset KI; Fig. 1a–c ). Overall, 52% of the units originated from the PFC and 48% from other brain regions
outcomes.notes: On 001260 + 000473 (the paper's 99 recordings), reading (b) with at least 6 spikes in at least 12 spontaneous epochs gives 24,898 units (24,248 ± 2,425), 52.4% in the PFC (52 ± 5.2) and 13,040 PFC units (12,674 ± 1,267). Every other epoch rule under reading (b) is within tolerance too (25,929, 23,168 and 22,091 units; 13,559, 12,026 and 11,509 PFC units); with the paper's Zenodo quality flags 24,270 units remain. Reading (a) of the files' undescribed quality columns gives 6,561 or 16,545 units. 001260 alone holds 74 recordings and 17,205 units, 47.3% PFC.
deviations: The counts use dandiset 000473 as well, as the criterion allows; 001260 alone holds 74 of the 99 recordings.

Assumption. The files carry no quality label; reading (b), all units, is the main one, as the paper's own flags on Zenodo pass 97% of units. The epoch rule is the Methods' unit quality control ("≥4 ISIs in at least 12 separate 3-s epochs", not restricted to active epochs) with the Methods' "at least six spikes (corresponding to at least four ISIs)"; 5 spikes, and active epochs only, are variants, and all give counts within tolerance.

Assumption. Sleep-like periods are detected per recording session from the pooled 10-ms counts of the cortical units of all its probes (Methods, Detection of sleep-like periods, "detected per recording session ... across all cortical spikes"), and not at all in a session where the detector marks 1% of the time or more in a Poisson population of the same pooled rate (10 sessions of 001260, among them the four probes the code marks "ignore"), a rule of this attempt and not of the paper; the Methods say detection "was only performed for the dataset KI, as sessions of this dataset consistently featured a sufficient number of cortical units to detect collective off periods", which describes no skipped session, and the rule was chosen because the paper's own detection files mark 19 recordings off_used = no. The per-probe detection of round 1, the code's detector, the main detector without detection in the sessions the paper's files mark off_used = no, and the paper's own sleep-like periods (Zenodo) are variants.

outcomes.statement: Peak-to-trough durations are bimodal, splitting units into 19,186 ww units (81.1%) and 4,200 nw units (17.7%), with 862 intermediate units left unclassified.
outcomes.source: Figure 1h and legend; Results, Capturing the diversity of spontaneous firing patterns, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: As expected, spike widths were bimodally distributed, allowing us to distinguish ww ( n = 19,186; 81.1%) and nw ( n = 4,200; 17.7%) units (Fig. 1h )
outcomes.notes: On 001260 + 000473, reading (b), at least 6 spikes in 12 spontaneous epochs, there are 19,731 ww (19,186 ± 1,919), 4,247 nw (4,200 ± 420) and 920 unclassified units (862 ± 86); ww are 79.2% and nw 17.1% of all units (82.3% and 17.7% of ww plus nw). With 5 spikes the unclassified units are 951, just outside; with active epochs only the ww units are 17,239, just outside; with the paper's Zenodo quality flags all three counts are within tolerance (19,182, 4,181, 907). The peak-to-trough histogram has modes at 0.26 and 0.64 ms and a minimum at 0.36 ms.
deviations: Peak-to-trough durations are the dataset's Peak_to_Trough column; they agree within 0.001 ms with the paper's Zenodo values for 95.1% of units.

Assumption. Units selected as in dataset-ki-counts (6 spikes in 12 spontaneous epochs); the readings of the epoch rule differ in one count each, and this one is taken as it follows both passages of the Methods.

outcomes.statement: Narrow-waveform units have significantly higher firing rates, burstiness and memory than wide-waveform units.
outcomes.source: Figure 1i; Results, Capturing the diversity of spontaneous firing patterns, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: indeed, nw units displayed significantly higher firing rates, along with higher burstiness and memory compared to ww units (Fig. 1i )
outcomes.notes: nw minus ww is +0.245 in log10FR, +0.051 in B and +0.042 in M, p ≤ 4.5e-84 for each, 12,112 ww and 2,949 nw units from 41 mice. Same sign in every setting and without units of log10FR < 0.1 (p ≤ 7.2e-66).
deviations: Mixed models fitted by REML in statsmodels and tested by the Wald test of the unit-type coefficient; the paper's Kenward-Roger F test is not available there.
Data of 001260 only (74 of 99 recordings).

outcomes.statement: Firing metrics in sleep-like epochs differ from those in active spontaneous epochs, which is why sleep-like epochs are excluded.
outcomes.source: Results, Capturing the diversity of spontaneous firing patterns, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 1d,e
outcomes.quote: Epochs contaminated by ‘sleep-like’ periods 27 were excluded due to their fundamentally different, nonstationary firing characteristics
outcomes.notes: With the main detector, sleep-like minus active in ww units is +0.031 in B (p = 5.3e-63) and -0.011 in M (p = 2.3e-12), but +0.008 in log10FR (p = 0.14), from 12,112 active and 8,405 sleep-like samples; two of three metrics. The same with no detection where the paper's files say off_used = no (log10FR p = 0.41). With the detector per probe, the code's detector, or the paper's own sleep-like periods from Zenodo all three differ (log10FR p = 4.4e-06, 0.0012, 0.0027), log10FR with changing sign (-0.024, +0.018, +0.019); B and M differ the same way under every detector.

outcomes.statement: Sleep-like episodes occupy a median 6% (IQR 0 to 18%) of recording time; sessions hold a median 227 (IQR 172 to 284) spontaneous active epochs and 19 (IQR 1 to 84) sleep-like epochs.
outcomes.source: Methods, Detection of sleep-like periods and Epoch selection; Extended Data Fig. 1 legend, Data (unit count)
outcomes.quote: Sleep-like episodes occupied 6% (IQR, 0–18%) of the time in recording sessions ... Recording sessions contained 227 (IQR, 172–284) spontaneous active epochs and 19 (IQR, 1–84) sleep-like epochs
outcomes.notes: With the main detector, sleep-like time per probe recording has a median 9.9% (IQR 2.7 to 20.3%), active epochs 215 (within 227 ± 22.7) and sleep-like epochs 73.5 (19 expected); 8,405 ww units have at least 12 sleep-like epochs (11,599 ± 1,160). Per session 10.5%, 207, 73.5. Per probe 20.0%, 180, 125; the code's detector 8.7%, 203, 83.5; the paper's own sleep-like periods on Zenodo 1.5%, 248, 21.5 on these recordings. The paper's own detection files give a median quiet time of 5.3% (IQR 0.7 to 17.2%) over 73 recordings and mark 19 as off_used = no; where the paper used detection the main detector marks 15.9%, where it did not 3.1% (Spearman 0.65 with the paper's values). With fewer than 75 cortical units the per-probe detector marks 84.5% of the time against 33.3% for a Poisson null; from 75 units the null marks 0.1% or less while the detector marks 16 to 21%. The EMG is lower in detected periods (median ratio 0.9, IQR 0.8 to 1.0, 62 recordings). In 000473 the main detector marks 15.1%.
deviations: Recording time is from the first to the last spike.

outcomes.statement: Across ww units, a linear correlation does not reveal a dependence between burstiness and memory.
outcomes.source: Results, Brain regions have distinct firing repertoires, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 1f,g
outcomes.quote: Note that linear correlation did not reveal this empirical dependence between burstiness and memory (Extended Data Fig. 1f,g )
outcomes.notes: By the paper's test, B ~ M + (1|Mouse) across 12,112 ww units, the slope is -0.197 with p = 7.0e-75. The effect is small, marginal R2 0.025 (Pearson r -0.173); with thousands of units a small dependence is significant.
deviations: Wald test in statsmodels in place of the paper's test as implemented in Julia.

outcomes.statement: On the ww SOM, burstiness and firing rate vary along perpendicular gradients, while high memory occurs only with medium to low burstiness, so high memory and high burstiness are mutually exclusive.
outcomes.source: Figure 2a; Results, Brain regions have distinct firing repertoires, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: The SOM displayed perpendicular gradients of burstiness and firing rate, showing that these two metrics vary independently of each other. In contrast, high memory patches coincided with medium to low burstiness, indicating that high memory and high burstiness are mutually exclusive
outcomes.notes: The gradients of B and log10FR across the ww SOM are at 109.8 degrees (part 1 holds). Of the top 10% memory nodes 4 of 43, and of the top 25% 24 of 107, lie in the top quartile of node B, where the criterion asks for none (part 2 fails under both readings). The criterion defines no partial outcome; partially reproduced is used as the claim holds in part, with both readings agreeing.
deviations: The SOM grid is 17 by 25 (425 nodes), as the code's shape rule gives from 400.

outcomes.statement: PFC ww units are widely spread on the SOM, with many matching regular-firing (low burstiness) nodes and few in anti-memory territory, while units from other regions populate different territories.
outcomes.source: Figure 2b; Extended Data Fig. 2e; Results, Brain regions have distinct firing repertoires, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Overall, PFC units were widely distributed on the SOM, with many units matching best to regular firing (that is, low burstiness) and avoiding anti-memory territories (Fig. 2b ), while units from other brain regions populated different territories
outcomes.notes: PFC units are 49.4% of the 12,112 ww SOM units and hit all 425 nodes. Median B is -0.049 in PFC against -0.017 elsewhere (Mann-Whitney p = 5.3e-36); M < 0 in 56.0% against 69.3% (chi-square p = 1.5e-51). In the Aversion setting the B difference reverses (-0.076 against -0.096).

outcomes.statement: About 57% of ww units keep their category from one block of about 50 spontaneous epochs to the next, far above the 18% expected by chance from the marginal distributions.
outcomes.source: Figure 2e; Results, Stable classification of single-unit firing patterns, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Consistently, around 57% of units remained in the category they had in the previous block, which is considerably above the 18% expected from chance (marginal distributions; Fig. 2e )
outcomes.notes: Stability is 58.0% averaged over 13 transitions (58.5% for the pooled matrix), against 16.7% from the marginals (16.0% pooled, just below 16.2); each transition lies between 54.3% and 60.9%. With the code's minimum of 3 valid epochs per block it is 50.4% (chance 14.8%). Stability does not depend on the category numbering.
deviations: Assumption. Inherent blocks are runs of the trials table's Block column (20 recordings, where its runs have a median of at least 20 trials), runs of more than 75 epochs split in two; elsewhere consecutive blocks of 50 onsets. The files do not say which settings had blocks, and in Detection files the column holds the trial outcome. Blocks have a median of 27 valid epochs (paper 36).

Assumption. Sleep-like periods are detected per recording session from the pooled 10-ms counts of the cortical units of all its probes (Methods, Detection of sleep-like periods, "detected per recording session ... across all cortical spikes"), and not at all in a session where the detector marks 1% of the time or more in a Poisson population of the same pooled rate (10 sessions of 001260, among them the four probes the code marks "ignore"), a rule of this attempt and not of the paper; the Methods say detection "was only performed for the dataset KI, as sessions of this dataset consistently featured a sufficient number of cortical units to detect collective off periods", which describes no skipped session, and the rule was chosen because the paper's own detection files mark 19 recordings off_used = no. outcomes.statement: Block-wise category assignment is less stable for low-rate categories (1 to 3, 7 and 8) than for high-rate categories, and low-rate regular categories 1 to 3 mostly transition among themselves, as do the low-rate bursty categories 7 and 8.
outcomes.source: Figure 2f; Extended Data Fig. 3d; Results, Stable classification of single-unit firing patterns, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Indeed, the block-wise assignment of categories to units was substantially less stable for low-rate categories (1–3, 7 and 8) compared to high-rate categories (Fig. 2f and Extended Data Fig. 3d ) ... low-rate, regular-firing categories (1–3) mostly transitioned among themselves, as did the low-rate, bursty categories (7 and 8)
outcomes.notes: Under both G2 readings part 1 holds and part 2 fails, so they agree. Mean diagonal of P is 0.520 for categories 1 to 3, 7 and 8 against 0.575 for 4 to 6 under G2 a, 0.444 against 0.702 under G2 b, the coincidence diagonal agreeing. Within-group transitions exceed every single outside category for 1, 2 and 3 but not for 7 and 8 (G2 a) or 7 (G2 b). It rests on fig2e-category-stability's assumed blocks. With the round-1 per-probe sleep-like detection, which changes the units and the retrained clusters, the outcome was blocked (G2 readings differed). With the paper's own sleep-like periods (Zenodo, variant) the outcome is the same.
deviations: Blocks as in fig2e-category-stability (assumption).

outcomes.statement: Superficial cortical layers (L2/3) are enriched in bursty ww units, while deep layers (L5 to 6) are enriched in regular-firing ww units.

outcomes.quote: E-score analysis of ww unit activity revealed substantial enrichment in bursty units in the superficial cortical layers (L2/3), while deep cortical layers (L5–6) were enriched in regular-firing units
outcomes.notes: Under both G1 and both G2 readings, L2/3 is significantly enriched in bursty categories (G2 a 6 and 7, E = 4.0 to 4.2; G2 b 6 and 8, 1.8 to 4.0) and L6 in regular category 2 (2.4 to 2.6), but L5 has no significant positive E-score in categories 1 to 3 (at most 1.5). The readings agree; two of three parts hold. With the round-1 per-probe sleep-like detection, which changes the units and the retrained clusters, the outcome was blocked (G2 readings differed). With the paper's own sleep-like periods (Zenodo, variant) the outcome is the same.

outcomes.statement: ILA and PL are both strongly and significantly enriched in the most regular-firing category 1.
outcomes.source: Figure 2g; Supplementary Table 3 (not read); Results, Enrichment of low-rate, regular-firing units in the PFC, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Interestingly, ILA and PL were both heavily and significantly enriched in units of the most regular-firing category 1 (Supplementary Table 3 )
outcomes.notes: Under G2 b, ILA is significantly enriched in category 1 (E = 7.7 to 7.8) and PL is not (-0.1 to -0.2), partially reproduced; under G2 a both are depleted (ILA -5.1, PL -3.6), not reproduced. Blocked as its outcome differs under G2 (claims file). With the paper's own SOM (variant) both are enriched (ILA 10.6 to 11.0, PL 9.1 to 9.2).

outcomes.statement: ORBl, MOs and AIv are significantly enriched in bursty category 8 units, setting them apart from the activity-defined prefrontal entity.
outcomes.source: Figure 2g,h; Results, Enrichment of low-rate, regular-firing units in the PFC, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The ORBl, MOs and AIv, in contrast, were significantly enriched in bursty category 8 units
outcomes.notes: Under G2 b, ORBl (E = 1.9, P 0.041 to 0.044) and MOs (4.7 to 4.8) are enriched in category 8, AIv not; under G2 a none is (AIv depleted, -1.9 to -2.2). Blocked as its outcome differs under G2. With the paper's own SOM (variant) all three are enriched (5.5, 3.3 to 3.4, 4.5 to 4.6).

outcomes.source: Figure 2g; Results, Enrichment of low-rate, regular-firing units in the PFC, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Other brain regions like thalamus (TH) and hippocampal formation (HPF) were heavily and significantly enriched in bursty units (categories 6–8)
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), each of 6, 7 and 8, holds for neither region under any reading. Reading (b) holds for both under G2 b (TH 6, E = 9.5 to 10.1; HPF 8, 3.1 to 3.5), and under G2 a for HPF only (7, 3.1 to 3.5). The claim's readings disagree under G2 b and the outcome differs under G2. The paper's own SOM (variant) gives the same as G2 b.

outcomes.statement: Regional enrichment profiles of dataset KI are highly similar to those of dataset IBL Passive; for category 1, enrichment across 14 cortical (sub)regions correlates between the two datasets.
outcomes.source: Figure 2i; Extended Data Fig. 4; Results, Enrichment of low-rate, regular-firing units in the PFC, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Repeating the analyses with spontaneous activity obtained from the International Brain Laboratory (dataset IBL Passive 31 ) revealed a high degree of similarity between the regional enrichment profiles of the two datasets
outcomes.notes: Needs the spontaneous blocks of the 303 IBL Passive recordings from the IBL Brain Wide Map, spike-sorted per probe, to be fetched and processed. Not started in this run; fetching them would not fit the run's five hours alongside the dataset KI analyses or the notebook's 60-minute limit. It also depends on fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment, which is reproduced.

outcomes.quote: we observed that brain (sub)regions enriched in low-rate, regular-firing ww units were enriched in high-rate, regular-firing nw units. Similarly, regions enriched in low-rate, bursty ww units were enriched in high-rate, bursty nw units
outcomes.notes: Across 21 regions (9 in the paper) the mean r between ww categories 1 to 3 and the regular nw category is -0.070 to -0.025, not positive, under every reading; the mean r between ww 7 and 8 and the bursty nw category is 0.016 to 0.264. Over the 9 regions with the most nw units they are -0.131 to 0.002 and -0.157 to 0.215 (negative under G2 a). The regular part fails everywhere and the bursty part depends on the region set and G2.

outcomes.statement: In dataset KI, enrichment of cortical (sub)regions in low-rate, regular-firing units (categories 1 to 3, category 2 shown) correlates positively with the Harris cortical hierarchy score, driven by the split between low-hierarchy sensory regions and high-hierarchy PFC subregions.
outcomes.source: Figure 3a,c; Extended Data Fig. 6a; Results, Enrichment in units displaying regular spontaneous firing reflects high cortical hierarchy, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: We found a positive correlation between cortical hierarchy and enrichment in low-rate, regular-firing units (categories 1–3). This positive correlation was not driven by a continuous relationship but due to a bimodal distribution of hierarchical scores
outcomes.notes: Across 16 cortical areas (17 in the paper) category 2 enrichment correlates with the Harris score at r = 0.61 (p = 0.012) with groups and 0.64 (p = 0.007) without, under both G2 readings. With the paper's own sleep-like periods (Zenodo, variant) the outcome still differs under G2 (category 2 r = 0.56, p 0.023 to 0.024, with 1 and 3 positive under G2 b; r = -0.35 to -0.32 under G2 a).

outcomes.statement: Deep-layer PFC ww tone responses cluster into eight categories ordered by peak delay; most units have flat or negative responses (category 8), categories 1 to 4 have sharp peaks with consistent onsets, and categories 5 to 7 have variable onsets and persistent responses.
outcomes.source: Figure 5b; Extended Data Fig. 8a to c; Results, Tone response maps do not align with cytoarchitecture, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Most units displayed flat or negative response traces (category 8). Units belonging to tone response categories 1–4 exhibited well-defined peaks and consistent response peak onsets. In contrast, units belonging to tone response categories 5–7 had variable peak onset latencies and persistent responses
outcomes.notes: Under both training readings the flat or negative category 8 is the largest among 5,269 PFC deep ww units (3,837 and 3,019). The IQR of ZETA onsets of responsive units is 4.9 to 43.2 ms in categories 1 to 4 and 49.0 to 244.1 ms in 5 to 7. Recordings keep a median 139 tone epochs (188 in the paper).
deviations: zetapy 4.1 no longer returns the onset latency; it is computed from zetapy's instantaneous rate as the first crossing of half the peak height, as older zetapy versions did (a standard choice). Seeds are fixed per unit; 37 of 5,269 units had too few tone epochs for ZETA.
Working-memory recordings have no 10-kHz tones and are left out; 8 principal components explain 95.1% of the variance.

Assumption. Sleep-like periods are detected per recording session from the pooled 10-ms counts of the cortical units of all its probes (Methods, Detection of sleep-like periods, "detected per recording session ... across all cortical spikes"), and not at all in a session where the detector marks 1% of the time or more in a Poisson population of the same pooled rate (10 sessions of 001260, among them the four probes the code marks "ignore"), a rule of this attempt and not of the paper; the Methods say detection "was only performed for the dataset KI, as sessions of this dataset consistently featured a sufficient number of cortical units to detect collective off periods", which describes no skipped session, and the rule was chosen because the paper's own detection files mark 19 recordings off_used = no. The per-probe detection of round 1, the code's detector, the main detector without detection in the sessions the paper's files mark off_used = no, and the paper's own sleep-like periods (Zenodo) are variants.

outcomes.statement: Firing metric distributions do not differ significantly across behavioral settings.
outcomes.source: Methods, Habituation and behavioral settings
outcomes.quote: Importantly, although the mice were engaged in various behavioral tasks, firing metric distributions were not significantly different across behavioral settings
outcomes.notes: The paper names no test. As a variant in the notebook, Metric ~ Setting + (1|Mouse) for ww units finds Detection different from Passive in log10FR (p = 0.04), Aversion in B (p = 0.0021), Context and Detection in M (p = 0.017 and 1.3e-05); marginal R2 0.008 to 0.035.

findings.statement: Dataset KI is split across two dandisets. 001260 holds 74 recordings, 41 mice and 20,374 units; the other 25 recordings (25 mice, 9,408 units) are in 000473, whose title and metadata name a different paper (Esr1+ hypothalamic-habenula neurons). Neither dandiset says it holds part of dataset KI.

The two dandisets hold 29,782 units, the paper's count before its unit quality control, and no field marks the 24,248 units the paper kept. The paper's quality flags are only in its Zenodo metrics files.

The units table's two-column `quality` is described only as "ISI violation, false positive rate". Column 0 runs from 0 to 1.15e5 (median 2), so it is not the ISI violation ratio of the Methods' threshold of 0.1, and its definition is not given.

The behavioral setting of a recording is not a field; it can be read only from the session description and keywords. The flatmap position of each unit and the paper's ww/nw labels are not in the files and come from the paper's Zenodo record.

In Detection and Context files the trials columns `lick` and `valve` are described as "sound amplitude"; in Detection files `Block` holds the trial outcome (miss, hit, correct rejection, false alarm), not a block. In a Context file `sound` is False for all 524 trials though 524 tones were played. Every electrodes column is described as "my description".

For 283 of 20,374 units the location label in the files differs from the paper's Zenodo metrics files (207 of them in PL064_20200422-probe0), and the ww/nw label from the paper's differs for 3.0% of units when the Methods' thresholds are applied to the files' Peak_to_Trough.

The Methods detect sleep-like troughs below 0.2 of the geometric mean for longer than 5 ms; the code requires off periods of more than 50 ms and at most 0.6 s, pads only groups of at least 3 off periods by 1 s, fills free gaps of 1.5 s or less, and uses only PFC units with at least 75 of them. Both give more sleep-like time here (median 9.9% per session-pooled detection, 8.7% for the code's) than the paper's 6%.

Following the Methods, sleep-like periods take a median 9.9% of each recording of 001260 (6% in the paper; per-probe detection gives 20.0%). The paper's own detection files on Zenodo give a median 5.3% over 73 recordings and mark 19 recordings as not using the detection (off_used = no), a selection step the Methods do not describe; where the paper used it, the Methods detector marks a median 15.9% of the time here.

The Methods require "≥4 ISIs in at least 12 separate 3-s epochs" for unit quality and compute burstiness and memory in epochs "with at least six spikes (corresponding to at least four ISIs)", though six spikes give five ISIs. The Methods also say 99 probes were lowered and 24 recordings excluded, while Data availability gives 99 recorded sessions, the number the two dandisets hold.

Question for the authors. The paper numbers its spontaneous categories by its own Ward clusters (code, a memory ranking and a fixed permutation) and describes them in words; it gives no rule that carries the numbering to a retrained SOM. Under the code's rule and under a match to the text's descriptions the outcomes of 8 enrichment and hierarchy claims differ, and they are blocked. Projected on the paper's own trained SOM (Zenodo SOMs.zip), the units take categories that match the text, and 4 of the 8 claims hold. Should a reanalysis project units on the trained SOM, or which rule should it use?

Question for the authors. Which test supports "firing metric distributions were not significantly different across behavioral settings"? A mixed model with setting as a fixed effect finds differences here (for example Aversion against Passive in B, p = 0.0021).

Question for the authors. Which recordings had an inherent block structure for the stability analysis, and how is it stored in the files? The Block column holds block numbers in some settings and the trial outcome in Detection.

Question for the authors. The Methods say all sleep-like periods were reviewed visually; the paper's detection files (Zenodo quiet_active_detection.zip) mark 19 of 73 recordings off_used = no. What decided that a recording's detection was not used, and should a reanalysis repeat it from the EMG and LFP in the files?

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier tested epoch_metrics, escore, stability, coincidence and the sleep-like detector on synthetic inputs and checked the archive for the blocked claims. Report in transcripts/001260/verifier-1-report.md. Its other points: E-score significance is a 10% two-sided test (now said in the notebook); REML Wald tests in place of Kenward-Roger (unchanged, stated); the 425-node grid and the PCA variance (stated; 95.1% now).

disagreements.reason: Under the main rule (12 active epochs of at least 6 spikes) there are 20,354 units and 10,900 PFC units, both outside tolerance. The Unit quality control passage, the claim's own source, says "≥4 ISIs in at least 12 separate 3-s epochs" and does not say active; under that reading all four values hold.
The mean r between ww 1-3 and nw 5 is -0.001 to -0.077 under every G1 and G2 reading. 21 regions were used; the paper used 9.
Category 2 r is -0.17 under G2 (a), and 0.39-0.40 (p ≥ 0.135) under G2 (b). It is not significant under any reading. 15 areas were used; the paper used 17.
No category has p < 0.05 across the 11 PFC subregions under any reading. With n = 11 this is a weak claim of absence.
Both ILA dataROIs share a module, but that module holds 2 of 6 ILA dataROIs, so it fails both "ILA-specific" readings. This uses only 22 dataROIs, 2 of them in ILA.

Under G2 (b), ROIs 20 and 41 are in the top three. Under G2 (a), ROI 23 is lowest in 3 of 4 combinations of reference and G1. Reference (b) with G1 (b) and G2 (a) gives not reproduced, so strictly G2 disagrees in that one combination. The Gao table's highest scores are ROIs 5, 24, 3, 2, not 19, 20 and 41.
No ORBvl dataROI is significantly enriched in tone category 1 under any of the 8 readings.
The tone-responsiveness map is most similar to category 1 under G2 (a) and to category 5 under G2 (b); both are the same cluster. It is never most similar to category 8. The IBL parts are untested.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of round 2 with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the attempt record and the claims file, with the paper. Report in transcripts/001260/verifier-2-report.md. It agrees with all 40 outcomes. Its other points, the session-skip rule is labelled as the attempt's own; three sentences the outputs did not support are corrected (the fig2i notes, the settings finding's p-value, the Block column files in cell 40); the variant on the paper's own sleep-like periods was added for the claims whose outcome moved with the detector; the G2 numbering was added as a question for a reader.

entries.name: 001260-le-merre-2026
entries.title: A prefrontal cortex map from single-neuron activity (Le Merre, Heining et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Le Merre, Heining et al. (2026) on dandiset 001260, which holds 74 of the 99 Neuropixels recordings of the paper's dataset KI (the other 25 are in dandiset 000473). It recomputes the spontaneous firing metrics, the self-organizing map categories, their stability and their enrichment across brain regions, layers and the PFC flatmap, the Harris and Gao hierarchy correlations and the tone-response categories. The claims on the International Brain Laboratory data are not tested.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Le Merre, Heining et al. (2026) from dandiset 001260
